data.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** 231518b2b65a467e249ab3245c81103b63e8d5a8
* **Repo:** /Users/joeoakhart/digital-service-orchestra-worktrees/worktree-20260511-110427 (worktree)
* **Affected script:** `plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-pr.sh`
* **Affected workflow:** local session, `merge.strategy=pr`, `enforcement.strategy=ci`

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

In a local Claude Code session with PR merge strategy, `merge-to-main.sh` should drive an interactive loop in which the session agent is the LLM dispatch engine for any work the script needs done. Specifically, the local-mode loop should:

1. **Detect and resolve git merge conflicts** — when the branch diverges from main during push (e.g., another PR landed first), surface the conflicts to the session agent, let the agent resolve them, then continue.
2. **Monitor the PR CI run** — poll `gh pr checks` until all required checks complete; identify failures (test failures, lint, llm-review findings, security gates, etc.).
3. **Dispatch failure resolution** — for each detected failure, hand the session agent a structured task describing the failure category and the artifacts it needs (failing test name + log, llm-review finding + diff context, lint error + path, conflict files). Agent does the fix in-session, pushes, the script re-enters monitoring.
4. **Loop until green or escalate** — repeat (2)-(3) until CI passes OR a bounded number of iterations elapses OR the agent escalates a specific item as unfixable.

The local-session loop should reach the same end state that the CI-only auto-merge loop reaches when `_LLM_DISPATCH_CMD` is wired in CI: PR merged (or queued to merge) without manual operator round-trips.

#### Actual Behavior

The script fails out on the first issue it cannot resolve itself, and the session agent has to do every step manually with no orchestration help from the script:

* **Issue 1 — Unresolved threads / CI findings**: `_phase_resolve_threads` checks `_LLM_DISPATCH_CMD` at line 1050. When unset (as it is in every local session — the helper was deleted in S3 with no shipped default), the script emits `ESCALATE: _LLM_DISPATCH_CMD not set` and returns 1. Even if `_LLM_DISPATCH_CMD` were set, the next layer (`_pr_dispatch_unresolved_batch` line 660) checks `_dso_is_ci_environment` and emits a local escalation when not in CI, regardless of the var. So local sessions cannot use this code path at all.

* **Issue 2 — CI-failure remediation**: `_dispatch_fix_agent` (line 1406) has the same shape: `_REMEDIATE_LLM_CMD` required, plus a CI-environment guard. Local sessions cannot trigger automated CI fix loops.

* **Issue 3 — Merge conflicts**: `_phase_resolve_conflicts` uses `_RESOLVE_CONFLICTS_LLM_CMD` (line 1271, same shape). When unset locally, conflict resolution can't run. Observed in this session: the script created PR #89, the user landed PR #88 in parallel which conflicted on `.test-index`, and I (the session agent) had to manually fetch main, merge it, hand-resolve the duplicate-key, push. The script provided zero orchestration for that work — it just exited with the push complete and the PR in `CONFLICTING` state.

The net result: in a local PR-merge-strategy session, the script does exactly the part that doesn't need LLM dispatch (branch push + PR open), then exits. Everything else — conflict resolution, CI monitoring, failure remediation, review-thread response — falls back to the session agent doing it free-hand with no shared state, no resume mechanism, no bounded loop.

### Root cause (design gap)

The script's contract for LLM-driven steps is: invoke an external `<cmd> <prompt> <user-message> <tier>` helper, parse stdout for action markers. That contract assumes the helper exists OUT-OF-PROCESS and runs to completion non-interactively. It does NOT model the local-Claude-Code case where:

1. The LLM dispatch IS the calling agent (this session).
2. There is no separate dispatch process to invoke; the work happens between script invocations, not within one.
3. The right protocol is: the script emits a structured \"AGENT_TASK:...\" handoff describing what to do, then exits cleanly; the agent does the work and re-enters the script (e.g., via `--resume`); the script resumes monitoring; loop until the script declares done or escalates.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* Affected: every `/dso:end-session` / `/dso:commit` flow that ends in `merge-to-main.sh` against a `merge.strategy=pr` repo from a local session. Today that means every brainstorm/preplanning/sprint/fix-bug session that lands its work via PR.
* Adjacent: `/dso:fix-bug`, `/dso:debug-everything` — these are the agents that would actually do the failure-remediation work the loop hands off to, but they have no input contract from `merge-to-main-pr.sh` for inheriting \"here's the failure to fix, here's the artifact to read.\"

### 6. Possible fix paths (analysis only)

1. **Interactive-mode flag**: add `merge-to-main.sh --interactive` (or auto-detect when stdin is a TTY / outside CI) that switches the three LLM-dispatch phases into a structured handoff protocol. Each phase, when blocked, emits a single `AGENT_TASK:` line with category + payload, writes its checkpoint, and exits 10 (or some distinguished code). Session agent reads the line, does the work, re-runs `merge-to-main.sh --resume`. Script picks up the same phase from checkpoint.

2. **Local-dispatch shim**: ship a `merge-to-main-local-dispatch.sh` that wraps the `<cmd> <prompt> <user-message> <tier>` contract by writing the prompt + user message to a file in artifacts dir, exiting with a \"NEEDS_AGENT\" marker, and the agent invokes the script with `--resume-dispatch <task-id>` to feed the response back. Heavier; more moving parts.

3. **Separate phase commands**: split the loop into `merge-to-main.sh phase=poll-ci`, `phase=fix-failure`, `phase=resolve-threads`, etc. The session agent orchestrates the sequence and does the LLM work between phases. The script becomes a state machine kit, the agent becomes the loop driver. Cleanest separation of concerns; most refactoring.

4. **Sprint-style adoption**: wire `/dso:sprint` or a new `/dso:merge-to-main` skill to own the loop. The script becomes a passive helper; the skill is the orchestrator. Matches existing DSO patterns; aligns with the \"skill owns the workflow, scripts are kit\" architecture.

### Recommendation

Path 4 (skill-orchestrated loop) is the most DSO-native and avoids retrofitting interactive semantics onto a script designed for non-interactive batch flow. A new `/dso:finalize-pr` skill (or extension to an existing one) would:

* Run `merge-to-main.sh push-and-open-pr` (today's effective behavior).
* Loop: `gh pr checks` poll → detect failures → for each failure category, dispatch named DSO agents (test-fixer, llm-review-responder, conflict-resolver). Re-push, repeat.
* Exit when PR is mergeable + green OR escalate a specific blocker to the user.

Filing this for design before implementation. The fix is non-trivial and the local UX of PR-mode is currently broken to the point of nullifying the value of `merge.strategy=pr` for local sessions.
data.title: [merge-to-main]: PR-mode local session -> script bails on first conflict/CI-failure/review-thread instead of looping with the session agent as dispatch
